messages.subject: modularity with different alignments
parts:
Hi,

I want to run a modularity test on my data and I'm not sure about right way to go about it. I want to use the covariance ratio via phylo.modularity. I have 40 specimens with 3D landmarks and a phylogenetic tree. On those specimens, I have two structures which have been landmarked separately with separate Procrustes alignments. I did this because they articulate and did not want artifacts from preservation or scan position. Is it possible to use the phylo.modularity function if the structures have not been aligned together? If not, how should I proceed?

Thank you for any advice!
Bob

messages.author: 4d71c6e24fb21497
messages.subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] modularity with different alignments
parts:
Bob,

 

Yes you can do that. You must first combine the 2 structures into a single 3D array using combine.subsets, and then phylo.modularity. Please see the relevant help files.

 

Dean

parts:
Hi,

Thank you for the prompt response! I am glad that what I have done has not been in vain. I have followed your instructions and 99% of it is working and I think I am missing a trivial step. I tried it with my own data and the Plethodon data, so I will use the Plethodon data here:

I combined my two alignments as follows to conserve centroid size:
comb.lm <- combine.subsets(head = head.gpa, tail = tail.gpa, gpa = TRUE)

Then, I used that as input for the modularity test function, adding a partition with 26 A's and 64 B's:
MT <- phylo.modularity(comb.lm$coords, partition.gp=land.gps, phy=plethspecies$phy, CI = FALSE, iter=499)

But it seems like the combining doesn't conserve names, replacing them with numbers, which combine.subsets doesn't like:
No specimen names in data matrix. Please assign specimen names.

Can you confirm I am going about this appropriately, and highlight the step I am missing?

Thank you,
Bob

messages.subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] modularity with different alignments
parts:
Bob,

 

Any phylogenetic comparative method requires that the implementation ‘knows’ which observation corresponds with which tip of the phylogeny. That is based on specimen names matching phylogeny tip names.

 

You will need to assign these to your data at some point. However, it also appears that presently, ‘combine.subsets’ does not keep track of those names if they exist (thanks for identifying this!). Thus, you will need to go back and assign those once the combined data are created.

 

Below is an example of how to post-hoc re-instate them as a temporary workaround.

 

Dean

 

#####  Example of issue and work-around

data("plethspecies")

 

new <- combine.subsets(plethspecies$land[1:5,,], plethspecies$land[6:11,,])

new$coords

 

dimnames(new$coords)[3] <- dimnames(plethspecies$land)[3]

new$coords

Dean

 

Dr. Dean C. Adams

Iowa State University

messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] modularity with different alignments
parts:
Hi,

Thank you! That makes sense. I ran the test on my data as follows:

#combining the two separate GPAs; there are 370 and 252 points for my two GPAs with 40 taxa each
comb.lm<-combine.subsets(paturon=pat.gpa2, carapace=car.gpa, gpa=TRUE)

#renaming using your instructions
dimnames(comb.lm$coords)[3] <- dimnames(car.gpa$coords)[3]

#running the test
mod<-phylo.modularity(comb.lm$coords, partition.gp=land.gps,phy=spider.phy, CI = FALSE, iter=499)

The resulting CR = 0.988 and P=0.002. In the paper where it is introduced, CR < 1 is more modular and CR > 1 is more integrated...CR=0.988 is right on the line! Given the significant modular signal value, this supports modularity between my two structures, right? For comparison, not using the phylogeny (not that I'd want to do that given I have it, but just for kicks) had the same p-value but CR=0.566.

And the plot is very odd compared to the Plethodon example, so I wanted to check that all of this is as it is supposed to be (my data left, Plethodon example right):


Thank you again - hopefully this will be the last of me pestering you.
Bob

messages.subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] modularity with different alignments
parts:
Bob,

 

As per my paper, CR values less than 1.0 indicate modular signal. However, values greater than 1.0 do NOT represent integration. This is discussed clearly in the paper: the CR is for modularity only (PLS is for integration).

 

As to your distribution, this is not unexpected. The distribution of CR values obtained via permutation will be ‘tighter’ around 1.0 as the number of landmarks increases. See simulation example below with randomly generated data.

 

Dean

 

y <- matrix(rnorm(100000),ncol=500)

gps <- gl(2,250)

 

res <- modularity.test(y,gps)

plot(res)
